patches_reviewed.subject: Re: [PATCH] btrfs: tree-checker: reject file extent items for special files
Re: [PATCH v2] btrfs: tree-checker: add qgroup status item check
patches_reviewed.patch_summary: This patch adds a check for qgroup status item consistency in the Btrfs tree-checker, specifically looking for items that are missing the 'enable_gen' flag, which is new after the simple quotas change.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer questioned the effectiveness of checking the flags of a given item, citing potential false negatives if squota is not used or if the size is small, and suggested an alternative approach to identify qgroup status items missing enable_gen

Reviewer Qu Wenruo pointed out that the tree-checker's principle is to verify every member of a variable-sized structure, and specifically noted that checking flags like RESCAN/INCONSISTENT may not be necessary for regular qgroups since it's valid for them to not have these flags set. However, he suggested adding a check in simple mode to ensure the RESCAN flag is not set.
review_comments.raw_body:
Yes, the reason is correct.

For those still running qgroups and have never disabled it (which I 
believe they are minority now), their qgroup status items will stay 
without the enable_gen member.

---

This is the common practice for tree-checker, remember that tree-checker 
is the "2nd best memory tester" to catch weird problems, not only from 
btrfs, but also bad hardware.

So the principle is not "this should not happen so we don't need to 
check" but "every member should be verified when possible".

And this is part of the common path for any variable sized structure, we 
need to make sure the added member is not beyond the item boundary.


Finally for the "why not look for normal ones missing rescan or flags or 
whatever" part, that's because for regular qgroups, it's completely 
valid to not have RESCAN/INCONSISTENT flag set, so we do not need to 
check that.

But this inspired me that, for simple mode we should not have RESCAN 
flag set.
I'll add this check into the next version.

Thanks for the review,
Qu

patches_acked.subject: Re: [PATCH] btrfs: remove runtime tweakable feature sysfs interface
patches_acked.patch_summary: This patch removes the sysfs interface for runtime tweakable features in Btrfs, which allows certain behaviors to be dynamically adjusted without using ioctl or mount options. The removal is motivated by the fact that some features are not at whole filesystem granularity and the generic features mechanism no longer makes sense. This change simplifies the code and aligns with a desire to converge on using only ioctl for runtime feature setting.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary:
Qu Wenruo expressed no issues with the current sysfs interfaces, finding them more straightforward and less prone to compatibility problems compared to mount options, but noted that there is a potential race condition with mount/unmount operations.

Reviewer noted that the original assumption about features being enabled halfway was overly optimistic, and suggested that enabling work should be pushed into user-space programs rather than the kernel itself.
review_comments.raw_body:
Personally speaking I have no problem with the current sysfs interfaces 
at all.

It's more straightforward, less compatibility problems compared to mount 
options.

The only down side is the race with mount/unmount, but it's not a big 
deal as long as we're only modifying a single in-memory flag/value.

---

I think the features interface itself is totally fine, just we were a 
little too optimistic on the features that can be enabled halfway.

Nowadays if we want to introduce some new features, we will be more 
cautious and push most of the enabling work into progs other than the 
kernel itself, and may not choose to allowing mixed old and new structures.

Thanks for the review,
Qu

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v4 00/14] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3 00/14] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface
[PATCH v4 00/14] nfsd/sunrpc: harden the netlink listener set interface

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 01/14] NFSD: cap the number of listeners accepted in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the number of listeners accepted in the listener_set function to prevent a userland request from spinning indefinitely due to a nested loop that runs under sv_lock with bottom halves disabled. The limit is set at NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024) entries, which is far above any realistic configuration. This change does not cap the number of existing listeners but rather prevents new requests from exceeding this threshold. The patch also adds a check in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners to reject oversized listener lists before taking any locks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 02/14] NFSD: validate transport name in listener_set before serv creation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a validation check for the transport name in the listener_set function of NFSD before service creation. It ensures that only supported transport names (tcp, udp, and rdma) are accepted to prevent unknown names from triggering a request_module upcall under nfsd_mutex. The check is performed in the nfsd_nl_validate_listeners function, which runs before taking the nfsd_mutex lock. If an unsupported name is detected, it returns an error with a descriptive message indicating the offending attribute.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 03/14] SUNRPC: keep the first error in svc_register()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register() function in the SUNRPC module to keep track of the first error encountered during RPC program registration, rather than overwriting it with subsequent errors. This ensures that an earlier failure is not erased by a later success or failure. The fix addresses a problem introduced by a previous patch that allowed further customization of RPC program registration.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 04/14] SUNRPC: bound the local rpcbind client timeout to 1s
series_items.patch_summary: This patch limits the timeout for local rpcbind client connections to 1 second. The previous default timeouts of 10 seconds and 60 seconds were causing stalls in NFS server operations, leading to hung-task watchdog warnings. By bounding the timeout to a single attempt of 1 second, the patch reduces the duration of these stalls, but does not eliminate them entirely. A more comprehensive fix would involve making the registration process asynchronous. The change affects the kernel's local rpcbind client, which communicates with the local rpcbind service over loopback or AF_LOCAL sockets.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 05/14] NFSD: report listener creation failures through extack
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) code to report listener creation failures through extack, providing more detailed error information to userland. Specifically, it records the attribute and transport name of the entry that failed and reports both after the loop, allowing for more precise identification of the issue. This change addresses a limitation where only generic error messages were provided, making it harder to diagnose specific problems.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 06/14] SUNRPC: report local rpcbind calls that get no answer
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to report local rpcbind calls that receive no answer, allowing callers to distinguish between failures due to a non-responsive rpcbind and other types of errors. The patch introduces new error codes to categorize rpcbind call failures into three groups: answered (with a specific set of error codes), never sent (with a different set of error codes), and no answer (all remaining error codes). A count of unanswered rpcbind calls is also maintained in the serv structure, which will be used by later patches to adjust behavior based on hard rpcbind failures.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 07/14] SUNRPC: stop svc_register() once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_register function in the SUNRPC module to stop registering programs and versions when the local rpcbind client times out, rather than continuing to try other programs and versions. This change is made to prevent unnecessary delays and wasted time when a program's call to the local rpcbind times out. The approach taken is to add a new condition that breaks out of the loop if no answer was received from the rpcbind client.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 08/14] SUNRPC: stop the svc_unregister() sweep once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the svc_unregister() function to stop sweeping for stale rpcbind entries once it receives no answer from rpcbind. This is done to prevent unnecessary timeouts and improve performance when a local rpcbind never replies. The change affects how nfsd services handle listener setup and cleanup, reducing the number of timeouts incurred due to non-responsive rpcbind servers.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 09/14] SUNRPC: stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the SUNRPC code to stop unregistering listeners once rpcbind stops answering. The original behavior caused multiple timeouts for each listener, which was unnecessary and inefficient. When rpcbind fails to respond, the patch clears a flag on remaining transport listeners, preventing further timeouts.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 10/14] NFSD: stop registering with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in the NFSD code by stopping registration with rpcbind after a failure in listener_set. The current implementation calls svc_xprt_create_from_sa() for each requested listener, which can lead to multiple registrations with rpcbind and subsequent timeouts. To mitigate this, the patch reads the rpcb_failure_count before creating listeners and skips registering with rpcbind if it has failed previously. This approach reduces the likelihood of prolonged lock contention on nfsd_mutex.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 11/14] selftests/nfsd: exercise listener_set request validation
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds regression tests for the NFSD_CMD_LISTENER_SET checks in the NFS server (NFSD) code. The tests cover various invalid listener set requests, including bad transport names, missing addresses, and malformed entries. The tests use a stub to simulate the creation of an NFS service and run in their own network namespace. The patch also updates the MAINTAINERS file and adds a new directory for the NFSD selftests.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 12/14] selftests/nfsd: add a per-netns rpcbind stub and the listener round-trips
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a per-netns rpcbind stub to the selftests/nfsd suite, allowing tests to run within their own network namespace. The stub serves as a minimal responder that answers RPCBVERS_4 and RPCBVERS_2 requests, counts accepted connections and received calls, and shares mode information with the test. With this stub in place, additional tests are added to cover various scenarios, including listener creation, addition, removal, and round-trips for TCP, UDP, and IPv6 listeners. The patch also includes fixes for netlink socket configuration and teardown procedures to prevent namespace leaks.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 13/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener_set asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests to the selftests/nfsd module to ensure that the listener_set request only asks rpcbind once. The patch introduces new constants and procedures, including RPCB_STUB_SILENT, which silences a call without sending an answer, and version_set_only(), which makes the server v4-only by clearing all versions before reading the request. The tests cover various scenarios, including stopping a listener_set request from registering after rpcbind stops answering, checking that unregistration is handled correctly, and verifying that multiple listeners are not registered unnecessarily.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v4 14/14] selftests/nfsd: check that listener removal asks rpcbind once
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds a test case to the NFS daemon selftest suite to verify that removing a listener from the RPC bind service only results in one call to rpcbind, even if multiple listeners are removed at once. The test creates a stub RPC bind service and registers three listeners with it, then removes them one by one while monitoring the number of calls made to rpcbind. It checks that the second and third removals do not result in additional calls to rpcbind, ensuring that the listener removal process is efficient and does not incur unnecessary overhead.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to harden the netlink listener set interface in the NFS daemon (nfsd) and SunRPC code by introducing early error handling, reducing unnecessary RPC calls, and improving timeout handling. The goal is to prevent hangs and improve overall performance.

review_comments.author: Jeff Layton
review_comments.summary: The reviewer suggested that the patches are a good start, but some of the changes may not be necessary. They asked for more information about the performance benefits and whether the changes can be made more incremental.
review_comments.raw_body:
nfsd_nl_listener_set_doit() matches each requested listener against the
existing set. The nested loop that does this is O(N * M), where N is the
requested count and M is the existing count. The loop runs under sv_lock
with bottom halves disabled. A userland request with a very large listener
list can therefore spin in atomic context for a long time.

Reject a request that carries more than NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX (1024)
entries. The check goes in nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(), before the code
takes any lock. The limit is far above any realistic configuration.

This patch does not cap M. Only the message size bounded N; real sockets
bound M. A listener_set result set is the requested set, so that path also
holds M at the cap, but __write_ports_addxprt() adds two listeners per call
and removes none, so repeated calls can push M past it. The worst case
under sv_lock is therefore 1024 * M, plus 1024 nla_parse_nested() calls.
Both interfaces require CAP_NET_ADMIN.

Fixes: 16a471177496 ("NFSD: add listener-{set,get} netlink command")
Assisted-by: LLM
Signed-off-by: Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org>
---
 fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c | 16 +++++++++++-----
 1 file changed, 11 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

diff --git a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
index 5331b89c4281..b6f4d66f612a 100644
--- a/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
+++ b/fs/nfsd/nfsctl.c
@@ -1995,21 +1995,22 @@ int nfsd_nl_version_get_doit(struct sk_buff *skb, struct genl_info *info)
 	return err;
 }
 
+/* Upper bound on the number of listeners a single request may carry. */
+#define NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX	1024
+
 /**
  * nfsd_nl_validate_listeners - sanity-check the listener list from userland
  * @info: netlink metadata and command arguments
  *
- * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that each entry
- * is well-formed: it parses against the policy, carries both an address and
- * a transport name, and the address is long enough for its family. Doing
- * this up front lets the callers below assume every entry is valid and
- * guarantees we make no changes when the request is malformed.
+ * Walk every NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR attribute and confirm that the list is
+ * not oversized and that each entry is well-formed.
  *
  * Return: 0 if every entry is valid, or a negative errno otherwise.
  */
 static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 {
 	const struct nlattr *attr;
+	unsigned int count = 0;
 	int rem;
 
 	nlmsg_for_each_attr_type(attr, NFSD_A_SERVER_SOCK_ADDR, info->nlhdr,
@@ -2018,6 +2019,11 @@ static int nfsd_nl_validate_listeners(struct genl_info *info)
 		struct sockaddr *sa;
 		int err;
 
+		if (++count > NFSD_NL_LISTENER_MAX) {
+			NL_SET_ERR_MSG(info->extack, "too many listeners");
+			return -E2BIG;
+		}
+
 		err = nla_parse_nested(tb, NFSD_A_SOCK_MAX, attr,
 				       nfsd_sock_nl_policy, info->extack);
 		if (err < 0)

--
